name: Radios
summary: Use radios when users must choose exactly one option from a small, visible set.
whenToUse: Use for one answer from a small set where seeing every option helps users compare.
Use inline radios only for short, familiar binary choices such as Yes and No.
whenNotToUse: Use checkboxes when more than one answer may be selected.
Use a select or autocomplete when the option set is too long to scan.
Do not preselect an answer unless it is a genuine, safe default.

anatomy.name: Fieldset and legend
anatomy.description: A fieldset groups the question and all radio options.

anatomy.name: Radio group
anatomy.description: A govuk-radios container carries the enhancement hook.

anatomy.name: Radio items
anatomy.description: Native inputs share one name and each has a unique ID, value and associated label.

anatomy.name: Conditional content
anatomy.description: An option may reveal one small, directly related follow-up region.

variants.name: Stacked
variants.use: The default for most radio questions.

variants.name: Inline
variants.use: Short binary choices such as Yes and No.

variants.name: Small
variants.use: A compact expert interface after testing target size and usability.

behaviour: Initialise govuk-radios when using conditional content.
Without JavaScript, conditional content remains visible and server validation remains authoritative.
Do not reveal complex questions or another radio group conditionally; use a new page.
Retain the selected value after validation errors.
accessibility: Use native radio inputs inside a fieldset with a visible legend.
Associate labels, hints, errors and conditional content using unique IDs and official attributes.
Ensure options remain understandable in source order and with styling removed.
content: Write mutually exclusive, non-overlapping options that complete the legend's question.
Use a divider such as “or” only to separate a distinct final alternative.
Keep labels concise and add item hints only where necessary.
